No severities/weights changed. | 2026-07-30 addendum #3 (approved by Jeff, same session): sec-07 depends_on_files was wrong (pointed at src/lib/tenant-query.ts, unrelated to PIN storage) -- replaced with the real 15 files the PIN-encryption fix touches. No severities/weights changed. | 2026-07-31 addendum #4 (per Jeff's explicit in-session instruction: "Start adding real, evidence-backed checkpoints for more of the unmapped 782 surface items, prioritizing Security and Finance routes first"): added 7 new checkpoints (sec-10..sec-13, fin-07..fin-09) covering 31 previously-unmapped Security routes + 9 files/8 tables (auth/session/PIN-reset, admin RBAC, audit/monitoring visibility, webhook/internal/cron auth) and 27 previously-unmapped Finance routes (invoicing/payments, bank reconciliation, expenses/vendors). Severities assigned by blast radius consistent with existing checkpoints in each domain. No existing checkpoint's severity or weight changed. | 2026-07-31 addendum #5 (per Jeff's explicit in-session instruction, after reviewing the Sentry/error_logs cross-check findings: "The notification-delivery-rate failure gets its own checkpoint, not folded into ai-03 ... Add it as its own item and flag it high-severity given it's been broken for a week"): added ai-06 (notification delivery pipeline health, severity 4) to ai_agent_communications, covering the real recurring unresolved high-severity error_logs finding from the 2026-07-31 cross-check (src/app/api/cron/system-check/route.ts's Notifications 24h check, failing ~daily since at least 2026-07-25). No existing checkpoint's severity or weight changed. | 2026-08-01 addendum #6 (per Jeff's explicit in-session instruction, deep finance re-verification + first-ever HR domain scoring): fixed fin-01/fin-02's depends_on_files (was src/lib/jobs.ts, the wrong file -- same class of bug as the fin-04/sec-07 fixes already recorded above; the real post_journal_entry()/balance-invariant logic lives in src/lib/ledger.ts). Added fin-10..fin-15 (6 new finance checkpoints) covering the money-spine posting core + today's booking-labor-double-post and equipment-capitalization fixes, commissions/deposits/refunds/chargebacks (post-adjustments.ts, previously flagged as skipped), the financial reporting endpoint surface, admin cross-tenant finance rollups, equipment/inventory/vendor costing + budget templates, and remaining misc finance utility routes -- closing the previously-silent 36-route + entire-money-spine-lib coverage gap identified this pass. Added a new domain, hr_workforce (10 checkpoints, hr-01..hr-10), covering team roster/roles, HR employee profile records, documents/requirements/reminders, notes, pay-rate management, time tracking, PTO, 1099/W-2 classification, compliance fields, and performance/ratings -- HR had never been scored as its own domain before this pass. Weight rebalance: finance_payroll_billing 20->15, hr_workforce introduced at 5 (weights still sum to 100) -- HR gets its own domain rather than folding into Finance because it has its own distinct routed UI/API surface (src/app/dashboard/hr, hr_employee_profiles/hr_documents/hr_notes -- not finance tables) genuinely separate from payroll math, even though the two domains share real data dependencies (employment_type, pay_rate). The 5-point weight taken from Finance (rather than spread across all domains) reflects that HR is the closest conceptual neighbor being carved out, not an arbitrary cut. This is a recommendation Jeff can revise the weighting on; the domain-existence decision and checkpoint definitions are the real content here, not the exact point allocation. | 2026-08-01 addendum #7 (per Jeff's explicit in-session instruction: Finance/HR are intentionally light versions integrated into the platform, not standalone QuickBooks/full-HR-suite replacements -- recalibrate the taxonomy to measure against that real target, not an unstated full-suite bar): re-worded hr-02/hr-03/hr-10's checkpoint names to state the light-version bar explicitly (fields exist and work vs. 100% adoption; minimal checklist vs. full document-management; customer-rating signal is the intended feature, not a partial stand-in). Added a new ledger score value, 'out_of_scope' -- distinct from 'not_scored' (roadmap item, not yet verified) -- for checkpoints deliberately not part of this product; compute-readiness.mjs updated to exclude out_of_scope checkpoints from domain scoring and report them in their own section, separate from real gaps. Marked hr-07 (PTO) and hr-09 (structured compliance/cert tracking, distinct from hr-03's generic checklist) out_of_scope -- both are MY judgment calls (Jeff asked for confirmation; no roadmap doc exists either way), explicitly flagged as overridable. hr-04 (HR notes) and fin-14 (inventory/vendor costing) were investigated for the same light-scope question and kept AS-IS (not reclassified) -- no evidence supports treating either as intentionally deprioritized rather than a real, if low-severity, gap. hr-08 (1099/W-2 classification) was explicitly NOT treated as a scope question per Jeff's instruction -- it is a live tax-compliance risk, fixed this same pass with a default-and-flag UI mechanism (src/app/dashboard/hr/page.tsx) rather than a hard blocking requirement at worker creation, keeping the rest of onboarding light while surfacing the risk for review. fin-13 was clarified as a testing gap, not a scope question, distinguishing it from the checkpoints that genuinely are about product-intent. No severities or weights changed in this addendum.

checkpoints.name: DR restore drill executed and validated
Admin RBAC & cross-tenant access control surface
Money-spine posting core (ledger.ts, post-revenue/labor/depreciation/equipment-acquisition) + today's booking-labor & equipment-capitalization fixes
Financial reporting endpoint surface (P&L, balance sheet, trial balance, cash flow, tax export, statements, chart of accounts, periods, entities, CPA tokens)

Admin cross-tenant finance rollups -- IN SCOPE, fully functional (confirmed correctly requireAdmin-gated); low score reflects a TESTING gap (no automated test coverage exists), not a product-scope question -- distinguishing this explicitly per Jeff's 2026-08-01 recalibration instruction, since not every sub-90 score is either "fix the feature" or "mark it light-scope."

Equipment bookings, inventory/vendor costing & budget templates -- INVESTIGATED for light-scope intent (2026-08-01): no roadmap doc or code comment supports "intentionally minimal" -- migration 2026_07_21_inventory_vendor_catalog_costing.sql's own comment frames this as feeding the budget engine "real costs instead of a hand-typed guess," i.e. built to improve job-costing/margin accuracy, which is core CRM value, not a nice-to-have. Kept as a genuine usage gap, NOT reclassified out_of_scope.
Misc finance utility routes (mark-paid, pending, receipts, payroll-prep, backfill, ai-ask, bank-connect, cleaner-income, job expenses)
AI-chat lead creation (phone given, no client match)
Crew-member deactivation cascade to future/recurring bookings
Sold-but-unscheduled Booking check (pre-existing, not this session's fix)
General client management (CRUD, lists, detail views)
Marketing pages (broader than the 6 review pages checked)
Web-chat / SMS conversational engine, live usage
Notification delivery pipeline health (24h success rate)
Phase 2 build-out (industry service lists, national geocoding, Projects-vs-Services toggle)
Team member roster (roles, active status, contact info)

HR employee profile records (employment type, comp, hire/termination dates, title/department, emergency contact) -- LIGHT-VERSION BAR: the fields exist and the API/UI correctly read/write them; 100% tenant adoption is explicitly NOT the target for this product.
HR documents, requirements checklist & reminders -- LIGHT-VERSION BAR: a minimal checklist/upload surface, not a full document-management or compliance-tracking system.

HR notes -- MY JUDGMENT CALL, no roadmap doc found confirming or ruling this out either way: kept IN SCOPE as cheap, low-effort light-HR scaffolding (a free-text note field is standard even in minimal HR tooling), not reclassified as out_of_scope. Flagging this explicitly as a call Jeff should override if wrong.

PTO / time-off requests and approval flow -- MARKED OUT OF SCOPE for the light-version product (my judgment call, no roadmap doc found either confirming or ruling this out; flagging for Jeff to override if wrong). A request/approval/balance-tracking workflow is a substantially-sized feature, not light scaffolding -- doesn't fit "light HR integrated into the platform," not "full HR-suite replacement." No table, route, or UI exists for it at all.
1099 vs W-2 classification in practice -- NOT a scope question (per Jeff's explicit instruction): a live tax-compliance-risk item that must be addressed regardless of how light the rest of HR stays.

Compliance fields (certifications, permits, licenses) as a DISTINCT structured feature -- MARKED OUT OF SCOPE for the light version (my judgment call, no roadmap doc found either way; flagging for override). The light-version need is already served by hr-03's generic document-requirements checklist; a separate structured cert/permit/license system with expiry tracking and renewal reminders would be full-suite territory, not light scaffolding.

Team performance / customer ratings of workers -- LIGHT-VERSION BAR (Jeff's framing): a customer-submitted per-booking rating signal IS the intended light version of this feature, not a stand-in for a missing formal performance-review system.
